title: Don't Build Slop (4 Levels of AI Agent Maturity) - Ara Khan, Cline
talk_summary: A Cline engineer argues agents should be built as explicit state machines, kept minimal (every added instruction risks degrading frontier-model performance), made easy to build/test via CLI so other agents can iterate on them, and managed through a Kanban board with cloud sandboxes for parallelism. The core practical claims are: prune prompts ruthlessly, treat agents as inspectable state machines, and use Kanban + cloud VMs to exploit being inference-bound.

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat every added instruction, edge case, or if/else branch as a risk of degrading the model, and periodically rewrite the codebase to strip accumulated cruft; they cite newer model prompts being far shorter than older ones.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single thing you add to an agent risks making it worse... just get out of the way of the model
takeaways.numbers: claims GPT-5.3 prompt is ~1/3 the size of GPT-5's in the Codex repo

takeaways.technique: Model each agent as an explicit state machine with named states
takeaways.what_they_do: They insist every agent is a recursive loop with a few conditions and end states, and you should always be able to say which state a run is in; complex runs are just longer traversals of that machine.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every agent is at the end of the day is like a recursive loop... a while loop with a few conditions and a few end states

takeaways.technique: Make the agent easy to build and test from a CLI so other agents can iterate on it
takeaways.what_they_do: They build a CLI harness plus agents.md/skills and CI so a long-running coding agent can build, test, and end-to-end verify changes to the agent itself in a parallel thread.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as long as you have something that can build and test the agent really well in the form of a CLI... let a long running agent run through in a parallel thread

takeaways.technique: Kanban as the agent-manager UX with state transitions on review
takeaways.evidence_quote: when it's like it needs my input, it will go through review

takeaways.technique: Cloud sandboxes per task for long, parallel, self-verifying runs
takeaways.what_they_do: They push heavy agent compute to cloud VMs so each task gets an isolated machine with no local dependencies, enabling many parallel long runs (including UI click-through QA) that return as PRs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can completely paralyze and have like a separate machine for each of them... no local dependencies like in the cloud
takeaways.numbers: cloud agent tasks cited running 15-20 min, up to 50-60 min

takeaways.technique: Preserve provider-native reasoning traces / API formats when routing
takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that sending reasoning traces in the wrong format silently degrades performance with no error, so they test each frontier API's exact expected format rather than assuming interchangeability.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you don't, the response would still work, except that the performance would be degraded, and you would have no way of knowing
